subject: Discovery recap & next actions — VPC, customer-managed KMS, air-gapped options
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 17:15:00 -0400
Subject: Discovery recap & next actions — VPC, customer-managed KMS, air-gapped options

Hi Alice / Ben / IT SecOps,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. Below is a concise recap from our call, confirmation of the primary constraints you raised, and proposed next steps so we can size a Private/VPC deployment and validate procurement constraints.

Call summary (what we heard)
- Workloads: regulated PHI workloads (billing + clinical decision logs) must stay in your VPC or on-premise cluster; no PHI may transit managed public infra.
- Network: strict egress rules; only outbound to specific internal IP ranges / proxy; hardware firewall between inference cluster and corporate network.
- KMS: must use customer-managed keys (AWS KMS CMKs) with key policies that restrict Redwood access to a decryption-only role; key rotation handled on your side.
- Air-gap variant: you may require an air-gapped deployment for pilot in a staging facility (no internet access) — file transfer via SFTP appliance or physical media.
- Success criteria: (1) ability to serve isolated inference with latency <150ms p50 within your VPC, (2) pass SecOps checklist for key management & audit logs, (3) deployment model that allows controlled software updates per your change control windows.

Current stack you shared
- Kubernetes (EKS) for orchestration; separate EKS cluster for regulated workloads.
- Internal artifact repository (JFrog) and private container registry.
- AWS KMS as primary key service; separate account for sensitive keys.

Questions / open items from our side (please prioritize)
1) Can you share a network diagram (VPC subnets, NAT/route tables, firewall appliances) we can use to validate connector options? Prefer the sketch as PDF or exported Visio.
2) Which AWS account will hold the KMS CMK? Do you require cross-account key policies?
3) For the air-gapped pilot, confirm the allowed method for image ingestion (SFTP, removable media, or internal image mirroring).
4) Any required compliance artifacts beyond SOC 2 (e.g., HITRUST)?

Attachments I’m sending: redwood-private-reqs-checklist.xlsx (checklist keyed to your answers), kms-integration-notes.txt (high-level integration patterns), network-template.yaml (example CNI + route rules).

Proposed next steps (timeline)
- By Wed 24 Mar: Acme to share network diagram + indication of KMS account (action: Alice / IT SecOps).
- By Fri 26 Mar: Redwood will produce a tight-fit architecture options doc (VPC connector vs. full private deployment) and preliminary cost/latency estimate (action: Rafael).
- Week of 29 Mar: Technical working session (30–45m) with your infra team to validate NAT/firewall rules and demo the on-prem packaging (action: joint).

If this aligns, I’ll open a HubSpot task and share the architecture doc after we get the diagram.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next actions — VPC, customer-managed KMS, air-gapped options

Rafael — thanks for the summary and for the clear next steps. Quick answers inline: 

- Network diagram: attaching a sketch (acme-network-sketch-v1.pdf). That shows the EKS cluster for regulated workloads, our perimeter firewall, and the segregation between production and staging.
- KMS: We'll use the security-prod AWS account (account id ending 1122). We require cross-account policies so Redwood services in a different account can perform decrypt with a dedicated role.
- Air-gap: For the pilot we can accept images via an SFTP appliance that drops artifacts into an internal registry (we cannot accept USB media on the host).
- Compliance: HITRUST is on the roadmap next quarter; for now SOC 2 + internal audit reports are required.

We have modest timeline pressure — ideally a pilot in May. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports bringing up the inference runtime as containers within our EKS cluster (preferred) vs a managed appliance? Also please confirm what audit logs Redwood can forward to our SIEM (CloudWatch/CloudTrail compatible or syslog).

I'll send the diagram as a Google Drive link as well.

Best,
Alice
Alice Jenkins
VP, Infrastructure Operations | Acme Health Systems
alice.jenkins@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next actions — VPC, customer-managed KMS, air-gapped options

Alice — appreciate the quick turnaround and the sketch. Answers to your follow-ups: 

1) EKS deployment: yes — we support running the Redwood runtime inside your EKS cluster (containerized) or as a separated managed Private deployment that attaches over a secure VPC connector. Running inside your EKS gives you maximum control over networking and patch cadence; managed Private gives SLA-backed autoscaling and simpler ops.

2) Audit logs: we can emit detailed audit events (request metadata, model version, token counts) to CloudWatch logs or forward to an external syslog/collector via a FluentBit sidecar. We also support pushing structured events to S3 for long-term retention and to feed your SIEM.

3) KMS cross-account: that’s supported; we will need the ARN of the role Redwood should assume. We will provide a template IAM policy and example key policy for your KMS team to review.

Action items update:
- Rafael: prepare architecture options doc + sample IAM/key policies (target Fri 26 Mar).
- Acme (Alice / IT SecOps): confirm KMS ARN and share any preferred cross-account role name; confirm whether CloudWatch push or syslog forward is preferred for pilot.
- Monica: can you schedule the technical working session for the week of 29 Mar?

I’ve created a HubSpot task and attached the initial checklist to that record: https://hubspot.company/contacts/ACM-4732

Thanks — Rafael
